fences.description: One or more arrays on a shared index axis, with pointers, dependency arrows and span brackets.
fences.example:
```array id=two-sum caption="Two-pointer sweep on a sorted array"
values: [2, 7, 11, 15, 19]
pointers:
  - {index: 0, label: lo}
  - {index: 4, label: hi}
steps:
  - note: "2 + 19 = 21 > 9 — move hi left"
    activeIndices: [0, 4]
    line: 3
  - note: "2 + 15 = 17 > 9 — move hi left"
    pointers: [{index: 0, label: lo}, {index: 3, label: hi}]
    activeIndices: [0, 3]
  - note: "2 + 7 = 9 — found it"
    pointers: [{index: 0, label: lo}, {index: 1, label: hi}]
    activeIndices: [0, 1]
    breakpoint: true
code: |
  lo, hi = 0, len(a) - 1
  while lo < hi:
      s = a[lo] + a[hi]
      if s == target: return lo, hi
      if s > target: hi -= 1
      else: lo += 1
lang: python
```

rows.description: Several rows sharing one index axis. Each entry takes the single-row keys above.

fences.description: Columns in value space: histograms, trapping rain water, largest rectangle, sorting passes, latency distributions.

```bars id=rain caption="Trapping rain water"

    overlays: [{startIndex: 2, toValue: 1, label: "1"}]

  - note: "The big basin between 3 and 7 holds four units"
```

```bits id=subsets caption="Bitmask DP: visiting city 2"
  - note: "Add C to the visited set"
```

fences.description: A mermaid diagram walked one step at a time: focus and dim nodes, reveal sequence messages, highlight code in lockstep.
fences.example:
```kiwi-steps id=write-path caption="A write through the pipeline"
diagram: |
  flowchart LR
    A[Client] --> B[Storage]
    B --> C[Git commit]
    C --> D[Index update]
    D --> E[SSE broadcast]
steps:
  - note: "The client PUTs a page"
    focus: [A]
    dim: [C, D, E]
  - note: "Bytes land on disk — files are the source of truth"
    focus: [B]
    dim: [D, E]
  - note: "The commit makes the version addressable"
    focus: [C]
    dim: [E]
  - note: "Indexes are derivative, so they come last"
    focus: [D, E]
```

fences.description: A linked list: reversal, cycle detection, LRU chains, random pointers. A numeric `next` is how you draw a cycle back into the middle.
fences.example:
```list id=floyd caption="Floyd's cycle detection"
nodes:
  - {value: 1}
  - {value: 2}
  - {value: 3}
  - {value: 4}
  - {value: 5, next: 2}
steps:
  - note: "slow and fast both start at the head"
    pointers: [{index: 0, label: slow}, {index: 0, label: fast}]
  - note: "slow moves one, fast moves two"
    pointers: [{index: 1, label: slow}, {index: 2, label: fast}]
  - note: "fast has entered the cycle"
    pointers: [{index: 2, label: slow}, {index: 4, label: fast}]
  - note: "They meet inside the cycle — there is one"
    pointers: [{index: 3, label: "slow,fast"}]
    activeIndex: 3
    breakpoint: true
```

doubly.description: Draw a backward arrow beside each forward one.

edges.description: Arcs over the chain: `{from, to, label?, side?: "above"|"below"}` — random pointers, child links.

showNull.description: Draw a null terminator. Default true.

fences.description: Hash slots, chains and probe paths: hash tables, caches, symbol tables, routing tables, or a plain unordered dictionary.
fences.example:
```map id=probe caption="Linear probing into a full-ish table"
mode: open
capacity: 8
hashOf: {apple: 3, mango: 3}
slots:
  - null
  - null
  - null
  - {key: apple, value: 1}
  - null
  - null
  - null
  - null
steps:
  - note: "h(mango) = 3, but slot 3 is taken by apple"
    activeKey: mango
    activeSlots: [3]
    probePath: [3]
  - note: "Probe forward: slot 4 is free"
    activeKey: mango
    activeSlots: [4]
    probePath: [3, 4]
  - note: "Inserted. α = 2/8 — plenty of headroom"
    slots:
      - null
      - null
      - null
      - {key: apple, value: 1}
      - {key: mango, value: 2}
      - null
      - null
      - null
```

mode.description: How to draw it: "chain" for buckets, "open" for open addressing with tombstones, "map" for an unordered dictionary. Inferred from `slots` / `entries`.

slots.description: One entry per slot: `null` empty, `"DEL"` a tombstone, `{key, value?}`, or a list of those for a chain.

entries.description: `{key, value?}` for `mode: "map"` — a frequency map, a seen-set.

hashOf.description: Key → slot, shown as an `h(k)=i` badge.

activeKey.description: The key being inserted or looked up this step.

probePath.description: Slots visited in order, numbered above the row.

tombstones.description: Slots holding a tombstone, if not already `"DEL"`.

showIndices.description: Index captions under the slots. Default true.

why.description: Slot index → explanation, revealed on select.

widgetId.description: Name for the inspect bus, for cross-widget linking.

fences.description: An index-addressed table: DP tables, grids, adjacency matrices, confusion matrices. Cells take `[r, c]` or `"r,c"`.
fences.example:
```matrix id=lcs caption="Longest common subsequence of ABC and AC"
rowHeaders: ["", A, B, C]
colHeaders: ["", A, C]
values:
  - [0, 0, 0]
  - [0, 1, 1]
  - [0, 1, 1]
  - [0, 1, 2]
steps:
  - note: "Characters match: take the diagonal and add one"
    activeCells: [[1, 1]]
    readCells: [[0, 0]]
    line: 4
  - note: "No match: carry the better of above and left"
    activeCells: [[2, 2]]
    readCells: [[1, 2], [2, 1]]
    line: 6
  - note: "Match again — the answer is 2"
    activeCells: [[3, 2]]
    readCells: [[2, 1]]
    path: [[3, 2], [2, 1], [1, 1]]
code: |
  for i in range(1, n + 1):
      for j in range(1, m + 1):
          if a[i-1] == b[j-1]:
              dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1
          else:
              dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])
lang: python
```

```numberline id=bsearch caption="Binary search on the answer: narrowing [1, 32]"
min: 0
max: 32
step: 4
label: capacity
steps:
  - note: "The whole range is still feasible"
    intervals: [{from: 1, to: 32, label: "candidates"}]
    pointers: [{at: 1, label: lo}, {at: 32, label: hi}, {at: 16, label: mid}]
  - note: "16 works — discard everything above it"

    pointers: [{at: 1, label: lo}, {at: 16, label: hi}, {at: 8, label: mid}]
  - note: "8 is too small — the answer is in (8, 16]"

    pointers: [{at: 9, label: lo}, {at: 16, label: hi}]
```

fences.description: A coordinate plane in data units: geometry, sweep lines, hulls, vectors, tile maps. Draws what it is given — the algorithm stays in the steps.
fences.example:
```plane id=hull caption="Andrew's monotone chain, lower hull"
xMin: 0
xMax: 10
yMin: 0
yMax: 8
points:
  - {id: a, x: 1, y: 1, label: a}
  - {id: b, x: 3, y: 4, label: b}
  - {id: c, x: 5, y: 2, label: c}
  - {id: d, x: 8, y: 6, label: d}
  - {id: e, x: 9, y: 2, label: e}
steps:
  - note: "Sort by x, start the lower hull with a and b"
    polygons: [{points: [a, b], open: true, id: hull}]
    activeIds: [a, b]
  - note: "a→b→c turns clockwise, so b is not on the hull — pop it"
    polygons: [{points: [a, b, c], open: true, id: hull}]
    activeIds: [b]
  - note: "Lower hull is a, c, e"
    polygons: [{points: [a, c, e], open: true, id: hull}]
```

fences.description: Spans on a shared axis with named lanes and causal arrows: scheduling, lock handoffs, happens-before, isolation anomalies, log spans.
fences.example:
```timeline id=lock caption="T2 blocks on the row lock T1 holds"
lanes: [T1, T2]
hoverPredecessors: true
intervals:
  - {id: t1run, lane: T1, start: 0, end: 4, label: "UPDATE", state: holding}
  - {id: t1commit, lane: T1, start: 4, end: 5, label: COMMIT, state: running}
  - {id: t2wait, lane: T2, start: 2, end: 5, label: "waiting for lock", state: blocked}
  - {id: t2run, lane: T2, start: 5, end: 8, label: "UPDATE", state: holding}
links:
  - {from: t1commit, to: t2run, label: "lock released"}
steps:
  - note: "T1 takes the row lock"
    activeIds: [t1run]
  - note: "T2's UPDATE blocks — hatched, because it is doing no work"
```

fences.description: Binary, n-ary and keyed trees: BSTs, tries, recursion trees, heaps (`fromArray`), union-find forests (`parents`), B-tree pages (`keys`).
fences.example:
```tree id=heap caption="Sift-down after popping the root"
fromArray: [1, 3, 2, 7, 5, 9]
steps:
  - note: "Pop the root; move the last element up"
    activeNodes: [0]
  - note: "9 is bigger than both children — swap with the smaller, 2"
    activeNodes: [0, 2]
    highlightNodes: [1]
  - note: "Heap property restored"
    dimNodes: [0, 1, 2]
```

root.description: Nested node: `{value, id?, badge?, edgeLabel?, keys?, leaf?, left?, right?, children?}`.

roots.description: Several trees side by side — a disjoint-set forest, a trie split per letter.

parents.description: Parent pointers instead of nesting: `parents[i]` is the parent of `i`. Self, `null` or `-1` marks a root. Node keys are the indices or object keys.

fromArray.description: Build a complete heap from an array: ids are indices, children of `i` are `2i+1`/`2i+2`. Pair with an `array` fence and `link:` for the two-representation view.

arity.description: `fromArray` children per node. 2 (default) for a binary heap.

withArray.description: With `fromArray`: also draw the backing array beside the tree, highlights kept in step. Default true.

badges.description: Badge per node key — subtree size, the range a segment-tree node covers.

nodeColors.description: Base color per node key, e.g. one per connected component.

prunedNodes.description: Node keys the search abandoned — drawn dashed and struck through.

highlightEdges.description: Child keys, or `"parent->child"`, whose edge lights up.

activeKeys.description: Which key cells light inside a keyed page: `{nodeId: [keyIndex, …]}`.

ghostEdges.description: Edges that no longer exist, drawn dashed: `{from, to, label?}` — the old link after a rotation.

edgeDirection.description: Arrowheads on edges. "up" for parent pointers and union-find.

nextLinks.description: Same-level arrows: `{from, to}` — next-right pointers, the B+-tree leaf chain.

pointers.description: Labels next to nodes: `{value?|id?, label, color?}`.

showNulls.description: Dashed empty slot on the missing side of a one-child binary node. Default true.

animate.description: Glide nodes to new positions when the tree changes. Default true.

hGap.description: Horizontal gap between sibling subtrees, px.

keyCell.description: Width of one key cell in a keyed page, px. Default 30.

link.description: Widget whose keys correspond to these node ids, for linked highlighting.

ariaLabel.description: Accessible name. Defaults to a summary derived from the data.

props.description: Escape hatch for a widget prop whose name collides with a reserved key.
